title: The result is narrowed to the low lane of INSERT(outside, lane, 0) even when the function wrote the outside (xor eax,eax; setcc al)
owner: r2ssa recover_interface.rs (plan phase PE); caller-demand narrowing belongs to P7's result proof
evidence: VERIFIED. crates/r2ssa/src/recover_interface.rs:759 calls narrow_zero_extend_input_size for the result. Its Insert arm (:790-794) returns the inserted lane's size whenever the position is 0, and never asks what the outside operand holds. pdim @0x401150 (branchy clang-O1 gate_three, stripped build) shows RAX_1 = COPY const:0 and RAX_2 = INSERT(RAX_1, ZF_6, const:0), so the rendering is `uint8_t fcn_...` for `int f`. Instruction addresses were verified by objdump for all 13 keys. Per-vector re-counts reproduce exactly: 13-48 vectors per record fail orig!=O0 and O0!=O2 together, and UBSan is clean in all 13. Control case: gcc-O1 gt (`setg al; movzx eax,al`) takes the ZExt arm, renders uint32_t and is equal. Correction to the latent list: the renderings graded 'equal' with the same uint8_t signature are gate_one and affine_probe at clang-O1, clang-O2 and gcc-O2, and mask_probe at clang-O1/O2 only. The same cause also: (a) is the grading cause of branchy clang-O1/O2 paired_sum_diff, which is not in this batch and is graded 'differs' because O0 and O2 leave the same garbage byte (00010000); (b) is a secondary defect of manual_limits clang-O1/O2 main (int main rendered uint8_t; epilogue `xor eax,eax; cmp [manual_sink],0; sete al`). Known-vs-new: critique:lowering (sext) and critique:calls F7 cite this function only for over-wide results; the under-wide direction is recorded nowhere. Gate note (confirmed): these 13 are 'differs' in substance. A disagreement in bytes above a narrow declared return is not C UB, but 'ub' outranks 'differs' (tests/equiv/gate.py:73, :378-380).
fix: PE: delete narrow_zero_extend_input_size, as the plan says, and never declare a result narrower than the bytes every return path defines unless P7's closed-world caller-demand proof says callers observe less. Refinement: after folding, `xor eax,eax` is `RAX_1 = COPY const:0`, a full 8-byte write. So a written-lane lattice over the folded SSA yields 8 bytes (uint64_t): sound but over-wide. The source-exact 4 bytes needs the lattice to keep the 32-bit write's ZEXT provenance, or to run before folding. Either 4 or 8 is sound; 1 is not. Reject critique:lowering's narrow(v) = 'smallest w whose higher bytes are proven zero' for results: it is value-exact, but it drops the defined-zero guarantee the original's callers observe, and here it would choose 1 byte. Regression: an equiv census in which all 13 keys, paired_sum_diff clang-O1/O2 and the latent 'equal' uint8_t renderings declare at least a 32-bit result. Optional gate change: when orig!=O0 also fails on the vector, report 'differs' rather than 'ub'.

title: Machine accesses with no effective-type or alignment proof are spelled as typed dereferences *(T*)p
owner: r2rewrite typed.rs owns C-operator admissibility and chooses the memcpy helper (plan P10). r2ssa supplies the address congruence (known bits or StridedInterval stride). r2dec memory_renderer only spells.
evidence: VERIFIED. crates/r2dec/src/fold/op_lower/memory_renderer.rs:973-978 is the generic `CExpr::Deref(cast(ptr(elem_ty), addr))` fallback; :818-821 (indexed) and :839-842 (slot bytes) have the same shape. 'align' appears nowhere in the file. x86 mov r32 and movdqu permit any alignment, but C *(uint32_t*)p and *(__uint128_t*)p require alignof(T) and a matching effective type. All cited rendering lines were checked. hashes unaligned_words (source memcpy(&w, p+i+1, 4)) renders `*(uint32_t*)(RDI_0 + RDX_1 + 1)` in five builds. review clang-O2 fill renders `*(__uint128_t*)0x404054 = XMM1_2` for movdqu to g_table+4. UBSan reports a misaligned load or store in every case (23-48 vectors per record), while orig!=O0 = 0 on every vector. Classification correction: no critique finding records this; critique:memory-model left 'memcpy vs pun' as an open question. The fix is, however, already in the plan: binding decision 2 and P10 'memcpy helpers where the effective type is unproven'. In both repros the effective type is NOT proven (bytes of a const uint8_t buffer; a 16-byte access into int[16]), so decision 2 applied as written already produces r2sleigh_load_u32 and r2sleigh_store_u128.
fix: P10 (implement binding decision 2): emit a typed dereference only when the accessed object's effective type is proven to be T. In ISO C such an object is aligned for T. Where the spelling type comes from inference or access width rather than a declaration, additionally require that alignof(T) divides the address's proven congruence. Otherwise spell the access with the static-inline memcpy helper (r2sleigh_load_u32(p), r2sleigh_store_u128(p, v)). Count each helper use in the proof line. Unit tests: stride 7 plus displacement +1 produces the helper; a 16-byte access at a 4-aligned global produces the helper; an aligned, declared array subscript keeps a[i]. Behaviour test: the six keys pass UBSan.

title: An indexed frame access whose index has no solved bound becomes a scalar object at its base displacement
owner: r2ssa: P4 memory partition (MAY evidence must merge, never mint a scalar) and P5 values (certified induction bounds must reach ValueRanges)
evidence: VERIFIED by re-running R2DEC_TRACE_REFUSAL pdd on both stripped builds. crates/r2ssa/src/semantic/shared.rs:1711-1716: first_reached falls back to unwrap_or(0) when values.lower_bound(index) is None, so the root is the raw displacement. shared.rs:1813: `let Some(bound) = values.upper_bound(index) else { continue; }` means such an access contributes no span, so roots.retain (:1847) never absorbs its root. shape_struct_array clang-O1 @0x4015e0: roots -72, -68 and -96; the only indexed-span-reach is root -68, bound=56, end=-8. The -96 root comes from the missing lower bound (rcx >= 3 would give -72); the separate -72 scalar comes from the missing upper bound. shape_stack_buffer clang-O2 @0x401750: root -73 for tmp:4e80_2 + RDX_2, and every span comes from the second loop's root -72. Here the lower bound alone (rdx >= 1) would have mapped the access to the existing -72 root. pdf @0x401750 certifies 'induction rdx = 0x1, +0x2 per trip (certified) ; trips 0x20 (solved)', yet ValueRanges has no bound for RDX. r2dec then declares `uint32_t stack_m72;` and `uint8_t stack_m73;` inside the loop body and indexes past them. The resulting out-of-bounds stores clobber the O0 frame: UBSan reports pointer-index overflow and index 17931 out of bounds, and gcc strict reports 'array subscript [6, 20] is outside array bounds of uint32_t[1]'. Classification: the shared.rs defect is recorded by no finding, but its fix is already specified by the known critique:memory-model 25.2 partition design (indexed I-intervals are MAY evidence clipped to the barrier window [b-, b+); escapes are merge inputs). Plan P4 deletes shared.rs:1741-1881 outright.
fix: P5: transport certified induction bounds (trips::max_count, σ-narrowing) into ValueRanges, so the two loops' indices get [0,56] and [24,80] (struct_array) and [1,63] (stack_buffer). P4 (memory/partition.rs): an indexed access with an unknown bound is MAY evidence that extends to the next MUST barrier. It never creates a root at its displacement, and the start must not default to 0 (merge, or refuse visibly). r2dec declares frame objects at function scope, never inside a loop body. Regression: shape_struct_array clang-O1 and shape_stack_buffer clang-O2 each render one 64-byte table or buffer and pass UBSan.

title: A self-recursive call takes its arity from the caller's register writes, because r2engine never prepares the root's own entry as a callee
owner: r2engine native.rs read_callees (orchestration; P6 bottom-up callee facts over SCCs), and r2ssa semantic/boundaries.rs for claiming an assumed arity complete (P7, critique:calls F5)
evidence: VERIFIED, with the cited mechanism corrected. The precise exclusion is crates/r2engine/src/native.rs:715 in read_callees: `.filter(|address| *address != entry && !callees.interfaces.contains_key(address))`. The root's own entry is never passed to prepared_callee, so no SourceCallSiteInterface exists for its self calls. recover_interface.rs:822-830, cited originally, is only the doc comment saying the provisional context lacks the root's interface. Trace (pdd @0x401b92, gcc-O0 stripped): 'call-site-correlation at function/mod.rs:1678: advisory Call at 0x401be4 target 0x401b92 prototype_arguments=None callee_interface=false', then 'call-boundary-fallback at boundaries.rs:1128 ... interface=false built=true arguments=3 results=1'. convention_call_boundary (boundaries.rs:765-803; arity rule :789-795) counts RDX, which gcc -O0 wrote as the temporary for b*3+depth before `mov rsi,rdx`. It then sets variadic=Some(false) and complete=true (:1141-1158). Result: `fcn_401b92(tmp_11f80_2 - 1, RDX_3, RDX_3)` against `uint64_t fcn_401b92(uint64_t, uint64_t)`, and gcc stops with 'too many arguments to function'. Other self-recursive functions (review clang-O0/gcc-O0 fact, shapes clang-O0 shape_recurse_direct) render the right arity only by luck: their bodies wrote exactly the argument registers. The F5 fix alone (render an assumed arity as a residual) would compile but would not give the correct call.
fix: P6/P7: recover the root's interface first, then bind its self-call boundaries to that interface as Exact arity and re-prepare. The self call's arguments are caller writes, not entry reads, so direct recursion converges in one extra pass. For mutual recursion, recover the call-graph SCC to a fixpoint (P6 'callee facts bottom-up over SCCs'). The caller-writes fallback yields only AtLeast(n) and renders a residual, never a complete call. Regression: shape_recurse_direct gcc-O0 compiles with a 2-argument self call and grades equal.

title: Equivalence gate: a rendering-run timeout is graded as an -O0/-O2 disagreement (ub)
owner: tests/equiv gate (gate-limitation). The contributing -O0 slowness is PE/P10 XMM lane noise.
evidence: VERIFIED. tests/equiv/rt/equiv_rt.c:857 gives renderings a fixed 4 x timeout_ms budget (4000 ms), regardless of the original's measured time. compare_runs (equiv_rt.c:577-579) records any outcome mismatch, including timeout vs return, as field 'exit'. tests/equiv/gate.py:378-380 then reports any O0!=O2 pair as ub, and gate.py:73 ranks ub first. review clang-O2 fact, vectors 37 and 45 (n=1190360900): original and O2 rendering return 0; the O0, pattern and ubsan renderings time out; the other 46 vectors are equal. Corrected timings, re-measured standalone with the oracle's .rodata mapped at 0x402000: rendering -O0 3.35-3.79 s, rendering -O2 0.25-0.31 s, source fact at clang -O2 0.39-0.47 s. Both renderings return 0 for n=1190360900 and 0x78 for n=5. The ~8x -O0 slowdown is real; the census's 0.88/7.3/2.1 s figures reflect a loaded machine, and even the original used ~90% of its own 1 s budget. The slowness comes from the vectorised pmuludq loop (9 pmuludq) spelled as __uint128_t lane-merge chains (44 __uint128_t uses in the rendering).
fix: Grade a timeout in a rendering run as its own non-blocking status (for example 'slow', with the measured ratio), and never as evidence of UB or 'differs' when the pair has a timeout on one side. Budget renderings from the original's measured wall time times a factor, with a floor, rather than from a fixed multiple of the configured timeout. Separately, PE lane narrowing removes the __uint128_t mask chains that make the -O0 rendering slow.

title: N1: the interface result is narrowed to an INSERT's lane although the base bytes are machine-defined
evidence: VERIFIED. crates/r2ssa/src/recover_interface.rs:785-803: narrow_zero_extend_input_size treats `Insert(base, x, position 0)` (the arm at :790-793) exactly like IntZExt and returns size(x), whatever the base is. recovered_result uses it at :759. For clang's `xor eax,eax; ...; sete al; ret`, the lift gives RAX_1 = COPY const:0 (the zero idiom as a 64-bit copy) and RAX_2 = INSERT(RAX_1, ZF_5, 0), so the result is declared uint8_t (re-run pdim; the headers of fcn_401180 and fcn_401170). A uint8_t return defines only AL, while the machine defines every byte of RAX (zero above bit 0), so an int caller reads garbage (equiv: eax 0x100 against 0). gcc's `sete al; movzx eax,al` of the same source is a ZEXT and stays `equal`. Two approved proposals repeat the defect. critique:calls F7's lattice states `wl(Insert(base,x,0)) = size(x)`, and critique:lowering's sparse_switch/sext narrow(v) ('smallest w with every byte >= w proven zero') would narrow the same way through known bits. The plan's PE line 'result width ... never from value ranges' already rejects the second; the first must be corrected before PE lands.
fix:
In the PE written-lane lattice, set wl(Insert(base, x, lsb)) = max(lsb + size(x), wl(base)) instead of size(x). wl(base) is the base's own written lane:
- IntZExt of a narrower write gives size(input) (the architectural zero-extension of that write, as in F7).
- A constant or zero idiom gives the full carrier: the lifter erases a constant's lane (F7), so the carrier is the only sound bound.
- Any other body definition gives its own width.
- Only an entry value of a register that is neither an argument nor preserved (unspecified by the ABI, proven by must-dependence from PE's dep()) gives bottom.

The result width is the max of wl over the returns. Below that, only closed-world caller demand (P7) may narrow. Known-zero bytes (value ranges or known bits) never narrow a result, because a C return narrower than the machine's written lane does not reproduce the zero bytes. Delete narrow_zero_extend_input_size.

Tests:
- `xor eax,eax; test; sete al; ret` recovers the full carrier, or 32 bits under proven caller demand.
- `sete al; movzx eax,al; ret` recovers 32 bits.
- `mov al,1; ret` with RAX an unspecified entry value recovers 1 byte.

Complexity: O(V+E) × lattice height 5.

title: N2: the INSERT lane mask `~(uintN_t)0` is subject to C integer promotion and erases the root
owner: r2dec lowering today (fold/op_lower); after P10, r2rewrite typed.rs owns the admissible spelling
evidence: VERIFIED. crates/r2dec/src/fold/op_lower/implementation.rs:2400-2413 builds `lane_ones = ~(lane_ty)0U`, casts it to dst_ty and shifts it by lsb. When lane_ty is narrower than int (uint8_t or uint16_t), C promotes (lane_ty)0 to int 0, so ~ gives int -1, which converts to all ones at the root width. `root & ~mask` is then 0 for lsb=0, and for lsb>0 it keeps only the bits below lsb. Either way every root bit above the lane is silently erased. siphash24's `xor dl,0xff` renders `RDX_15 = (RDX_15 & ~((uint64_t)~(uint8_t)0U << 0U)) | ...`, which zeroes bits 8..63 of v2. Reproduced (scratchpad/verify/sip): the gcc-O1 and gcc-O2 renderings match the source siphash24 on 0/40 lengths. With only the mask replaced by `~((uint64_t)0xffU << 0U)`, they match 40/40. The construct is latent in 27 more renderings that currently grade `equal` or `ub` (branchy gate_three, bool_relay and sign_xor; flag_materialisation classify and sum_carry; manual_limits out_param_parse, state_machine and table_walk; review sext O0/O1/O2; shapes mixed_touch and shape_stack_buffer; several values.c functions). They pass only because the erased bits are zero or unobserved. In review sext, `RAX_0 & ~mask` = `RAX_0 & 0` currently hides critique:lowering's entry-register read. A uint32_t or uint64_t lane is unaffected, since it is not promoted.
fix: Spell the lane mask at the root's unsigned width before shifting: `((dst_ty)(lane_ty)~(dst_ty)0 << lsb)`, or `((((dst_ty)1 << w) - 1) << lsb)` for w < root width. Better, emit one total helper, r2sleigh_insert_uN(root, lane, lsb), from r2rewrite's typed spelling (P10). Add an exhaustive proof harness over root widths {16,32,64,128}, lane widths {8,16,32} and every byte-aligned lsb that compiles the emitted C and compares it against P-code INSERT semantics. Add a Dylint that rejects emitted C applying `~` (or `-`) to an operand whose type is narrower than int. Expect the fix to move the 27 latent renderings: review sext will then really read the unspecified RAX_0, which critique:lowering sext (c) must refuse. Cost: O(1) per op.

title: N3: promote.rs takes an outgoing pointer-argument register for the frame pointer, so later address escapes are missed and escaped slots are promoted
owner: r2ssa (promote.rs; under the plan, the P4 frame partition becomes the single owner, with the frame-pointer proof from P3)
evidence: VERIFIED. crates/r2ssa/src/promote.rs:356-372 picks as frame_pointer the first register Copy in the entry block, after the first prologue step, whose source resolves to SP+k. In frameless clang -O1/-O2 shape_call_chain that is pdil op 45 `RDI = COPY uniq:0x4e00` (the `lea rdi,[rsp+0x18]` for shape_stash(&first)); op 24 `R15 = COPY RSI` does not resolve to SP. At op 45 itself (at == established), RDI is derived and escapes, so place 72 escapes. After it, is_frame_base (:382-389) holds for RDI. The later ops 67/91 `RDI = COPY rsp+0x10 / rsp+0x8` then skip the derived push in the Copy arm (:675-686) and the escape insertion, which requires !is_frame_base (:815-821). The refusal for a rewritten frame pointer (:533-545) is skipped because the function is one block that returns. Escape reach runs upward only (:841-852), so the escaped set {72} leaves 56 and 64 promotable. Trace: 'escaped base Some(72)' and '2 slots promoted out of memory: displacement 56, 64' for both clang-O1 (0x4013e0) and clang-O2 (0x401460). pdim shows the post-stash reload `COPY stack:m56_1` (the initial 0), so the rendering calls shape_step(0) and drops second*3 and third*7. The same path has a latent, unreproduced consequence: in a block that leaves, a later Load through the mis-chosen register (for example `mov rdi,[heap]; mov rax,[rdi]`) passes `is_frame_base(addr)` in the Load arm (:568) and is recorded as a frame-slot access.
fix: Take the frame pointer only from the prologue proof: `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp` or the AArch64 `stp x29,x30,...; mov x29,sp` shape, established before any frame access and never written again except in an exit block. This is the P3 item 'frame-pointer offset from the prologue proof', now consumed by promote.rs as well. Any other write of a frame-derived address into a non-Unique location is an escape, recorded where it happens. Immediate soundness guard until P4: in promote.rs, refuse promotion when a register write that is not the proven frame pointer copies a frame address after the chosen frame pointer was established. Under P4, promote.rs consumes the partition's escape and barrier facts instead of re-deriving them. Test (r2engine tests/native.rs style): an in-memory frameless program with three 8-byte locals whose addresses go to a writing callee via `lea rdi,[rsp+k]` in turn. Every post-call reload must stay a memory read, and no slot is promoted. Complexity: O(ops) per function.

title: N4: SSA construction ignores the implicit entry edge, so an entry block that is a branch target gets no phi (or a phi without the entry operand)
owner: r2ssa (domtree.rs dominance frontier, phi.rs placement, rename.rs phi operands)
evidence: VERIFIED. crates/r2ssa/src/domtree.rs:210-229 adds frontier edges only `if preds.len() >= 2` (:213), and the entry dominates itself (:65). crates/r2ssa/src/phi.rs:135 repeats the >= 2 filter at placement. Phi operands are one per CFG predecessor, and no edge supplies version 0. So when the entry block is also a loop header, it has one CFG predecessor and gets no phi. This happens with mutual tail recursion merged into one body (even `jmp odd`, odd `jmp even`) and with any function whose first block is a loop. Every use in the entry then reads the entry value, and the loop-carried definitions in the latch are unobserved and elided. Re-run pdim, clang-O1 shape_mutual_even: `Block 0x401710: preds: 0x401745; tmp:70500_1 = RDI_0 & RDI_0`, with RSI_2 and RDI_2 'elided UnobservedValue'. gcc-O2: `Block 0x401ab0: preds: 0x401a98` and `Block 0x401a80: preds: 0x401ac8`. Reproduced (scratchpad/verify/n4/t.S): `entry_loop: add rax,rdi; dec rdi; jnz entry_loop; ret` renders `for(;;){ RAX_0 += RDI_0; if (RDI_0 == 1) break; }` with 0 refused. The decrement is lost, and the loop never terminates for RDI != 1. A second repro with two back edges into the entry (t2.S) gets entry phis with no entry operand, `RDI_1 = phi([0x40110b]: RDI_2, [0x401113]: RDI_2)`, which loses RDI_0 entirely; that render fails closed with 'read_before_assignment'.
fix: Give the CFG a virtual entry node, or equivalently split the entry block with an empty synthetic pre-entry block whenever the real entry has any CFG predecessor. Build dominators, frontiers, phi placement and renaming over that graph. Entry values are definitions on the virtual edge, so the real entry is a join whenever it has a CFG predecessor. Phis are then placed there by the ordinary iterated-frontier rule, with version 0 as the virtual edge's operand. Consumers that assume 'the entry has no predecessors' must read the virtual edge instead: interface recovery's read-before-write, the promote.rs block-0 rules (delta and entry_adjustment), liveness and boundaries. Tests (crates/r2engine/tests/native.rs): the one-latch repro must render a loop that decrements RDI and carries RAX; the two-latch repro must render with a three-operand phi; and the two-function mutual tail recursion must render both steps. Complexity unchanged: O(E·α) dominators and O(E+V) placement.

title: N5 (secondary to critique:binding F1): a Store's C access width comes from a value type hint whose width differs from the op
evidence: VERIFIED. crates/r2dec/src/fold/op_lower/implementation.rs:2027-2030 sets elem_ty = certified_member_type_for_current_store().or_else(|| type_hint_for_var(val)).unwrap_or(uint_type_from_size(val.size)). type_hint_for_var (:1036-1073) returns the signature's parameter type for any value that crates/r2types/src/function_facts/mod.rs:331-346 maps to a Parameter slot, with no check that its width equals var.size. crates/r2dec/src/fold/op_lower/memory_renderer.rs checks the certified fact's width against val.size (:89), but then finalizes the access at elem_ty (:109, called from :161) without comparing size_of(elem_ty) to that width. F1's over-broad Parameter binding puts the 32-bit parameter type on RAX_2 = SEXT(reload of the EDI home), an 8-byte value (re-run pdim: RAX_2 is inline, and the signature is `uint32_t fcn_4017f0(uint32_t EDI_0)`). The 8-byte `mov QWORD PTR [g_note],rax` therefore renders as `*(uint32_t*)0x404030 = ...`, and the upper 4 bytes are never written.
fix: Invariant: the width of a rendered memory access is the op's width. A type fact may choose only the spelling (signedness, pointer-ness, member) of an access of the same width. In type_hint_for_var, or at the Store and Load call sites, reject any hint with size_of(ty) != val.size (dst.size for loads), and count the mismatch as refusal evidence instead of silently narrowing. Assert the same equality in memory_renderer before finalize_certified_memory_expr_for_fact. This is defense in depth; the real fix is F1's Identity-only reload certificate (P1), after which RAX_2 no longer carries the parameter binding. Test: `movsxd rax,[slot]; mov [g],rax` renders an 8-byte store whose value is sign-extended. Cost: O(1).

title: NEW-1: instruction-local p-code loops (x86 BSR/BSF/TZCNT, also PDEP/PEXT/ENTER) are lifted as Unimplemented, so every function using clz/ctz is refused
owner: r2sleigh-lift (internal_control.rs:44-47 and the conditional-skip else arm at :85); r2ssa obligation.rs:1485-1494 only reports it
evidence: CONFIRMED. The SLEIGH x86 spec writes BSR as a backward count loop (ia.sinc BSR Reg64 at 2842-2856: bitIndex=63, `if (ZF==1) goto <done>; <start> if ((rm64>>bitIndex)!=0) goto <done>; bitIndex=bitIndex-1; goto <start>`). TZCNT is the same shape (bmi1.sinc:179-194), and so is BSF (ia.sinc:2729-2744, bitIndex=0 counting up). internal_control.rs:44-47 replaces every local branch with target_index <= branch_index by R2ILOp::Unimplemented. The forward skip over the loop body is not speculatable either, so it also becomes Unimplemented. That gives exactly 3 per BSR and 2 per TZCNT. Verified counts by objdump: clang-O0 and gcc-O0 3 bsr + 2 tzcnt = 13; clang-O1/O2 2 bsr + 1 tzcnt = 8; gcc-O2 2 bsr + 2 tzcnt = 10 per lift, x3 lifts = 30 in the dump. obligation.rs:1485-1494 seeds VolatileOrUnknownEffect for each. On gcc-O1/O2 the same ops surface earlier as UnownedBindingSymbol through NEW-4. Scratch experiment (re-run): replacing every bsr/rep bsf with mov in the gcc -O1 assembly makes value_count_bits render (115 obligations, 0 refused), while replacing only the bsr still refuses. LZCNT and POPCNT are fine, because the spec uses lzcount()/popcount() there. Scope: the same guard also turns PDEP/PEXT (bmi2.sinc, 4 loops each), ENTER with a nesting level (ia.sinc) and the 16/32-bit BSF/BSR forms into Unimplemented.
fix:
In internal_control, recognise the bounded instruction-local loops, as block_transfer_from_repeat already does for rep-string loops, and rewrite each into a closed form over the existing r2il ops (Lzcount, PopCount, Select), keeping the spec's flag writes. CORRECTED formulas, with w the operand width:
- BSR: r = Select(src==0, w-1, (w-1) - Lzcount(src)). The claim's constant 63 is right only for the 64-bit form. The 32-bit form uses 31 and then zero-extends via check_Reg32_dest.
- TZCNT: r = PopCount(~src & (src-1)), which gives w at src==0, as the spec loop does.
- BSF is NOT the TZCNT formula at src==0. The spec yields 0 there, so BSF = Select(src==0, 0, PopCount(~src & (src-1))).
Prove each rewrite equal to the p-code loop: exhaustively at 8/16 bits, with Kani at 32/64. Judge the src==0 case explicitly for BSR/BSF: the spec's w-1/0 results are artifacts, since hardware leaves the destination unchanged (documented by AMD; undefined per Intel). Prove equality only on src!=0, and model src==0 as 'destination unchanged', or as a counted residual; never as a fabricated constant. Cover PDEP/PEXT (bounded by w iterations) in the same pass. r2dec renders the result through P10 total helpers. Separately, per decision 3, an Unimplemented op that remains should be a counted residual, not a whole-function refusal. That also needs NEW-4, or the residual would still delete every entry stack root.

title: NEW-2: SSE PSHUFLW (and siblings PSHUFHW/PSHUFW and the VEX forms) is an unmodelled Sleigh user operation, so vectorised byte-count loops are refused
evidence: CONFIRMED, with the description corrected. ia.sinc:8794-8801 declares `define pcodeop pshufhw/pshuflw/pshufw`, with XmmReg1 = pshuflw(XmmReg1, XmmReg2_m128, imm8:8). avx.sinc:2210/2218, avx2.sinc:598/606 and avx512.sinc:4635-4688 declare vpshufhw_* and vpshuflw_*. crates/r2sleigh-lift/src/disasm/user_operation.rs:273-293 (NAMED: NEON ops, traps, setISAMode) and PACKED_EXTENSIONS (PMOVSX/ZX) have none of them. In mem_scan2 clang-O2, PSHUFLW (imm8=0x50) widens the pcmpeqb byte masks into qword lanes (`punpcklbw; pshuflw 0x50; pshufd 0x50; psubq`). It does not broadcast a/b. The IL has two CallOther userop 157 (ops 160 and 242, imm Const 80) and no other CallOther. The refusal is raised in r2ssa machine/mod.rs:1852/1870 (MachineUse/WriteRefusal::UnmodelledUserOperation), relayed by the r2dec observation journal (observation_journal/mod.rs:200/282/592), and only spelled at r2engine lib.rs:2918-2923: 'unmodelled machine operation pshuflw at 0x4014c0:377'. crates/r2engine/tests/native.rs:1876-1920 already pins the same refusal class for pshufb.
fix:
Add ModelledUserOperation rows for pshuflw/pshufhw/pshufw and vpshuflw_avx/_avx2/_avx512vl/_avx512bw (and the vpshufhw_* forms) that expand into Subpiece/Piece:
- PSHUFLW: dst.word[k] = src.word[(imm8 >> 2k) & 3] for k in 0..4, and dst[127:64] = src[127:64]. The old destination input is ignored in the legacy form.
- PSHUFHW: the mirror image on the high qword.
- PSHUFW: 4 words over a 64-bit MMX register.
- AVX2/512: the same shuffle per 128-bit lane.
Cover it with an exhaustive test over all 256 imm8 values against a reference model, plus a behaviour test in crates/r2engine/tests/native.rs that the mem_scan2-shaped loop renders. More generally, decision 3 residuals should replace whole-function refusal for any user operation that stays unmodelled.

title: NEW-3: a stack-pointer carrier value used as data (the address of the frame object at SP+k) is given a C binding, and its CallRestore copies are then recorded twice (ConflictingWrite)
owner: r2ssa stack geometry (semantic/certificates/stack.rs:903-955) together with the P4 frame partition, which owns 'value v = &O + k'. The disposition rule is r2dec binding_plan: never bind a stack-pointer carrier value. observation_journal only exposes the conflict.
evidence:
CONFIRMED and REPRODUCED (scratch exp/p2p.c, gcc -O1, straight_calls at fcn.4011db, no loop: refused with ConflictingWrite(InstId(62))). CORRECTED MECHANISM: the `&O` spelling already exists. The write projection for RSP_2 is `AddrOf(Var(<frame object>))` (fold/op_lower/lowering.rs:417). What goes wrong:
(1) When the carrier's own value is a data operand (gcc `mov [rsp+0x10],rsp`, clang `mov rax,rsp; mov [rsp+0x20],rax` with the copy forwarded, gcc-O2 `movq xmm0,rsp` = IntZExt), the geometry certificate evicts it, and the eviction cascades back through the carrier chain (trace: 'ValueId(2) leaves the geometry: read ... by IntSub RSP_1 = RSP_0 - 8', stack.rs:931).
(2) r2dec binds the chain: 'ValueId(8) value_disposition=Some(Bound { binding: BindingId(0) })'.
(3) stack_base_absorbed_by (observation_journal/mod.rs:3070-3098) refuses to absorb it: 'not absorbed: this rendering spells it'.
(4) The CallRestore RSP_{n+2} = RSP_n has input and output in one binding, so it is marked a coalesced program copy (mod.rs:2419-2438) and recorded as an elided CoalescedCopy write (recording.rs:125-129). Its output also carries a rendered write observation (sealing.rs:215-232). record_same then fails with ConflictingWrite (sealing.rs:966-970), and the gap retry (lib.rs:3147) fails identically.
Uses of `lea [rsp+k]` also evict the carrier from the geometry (trace: 'RSP_4 leaves the geometry: read ... by IntAdd tmp = 0x10 + RSP_4'). Those still render, because the carrier's binding is never spelled and is absorbed. The discriminator is that the carrier's own value is spelled. Not in the known findings: the journal and findings index have no SP-carrier/absorption/ConflictingWrite entry.
fix: State 'this carrier value is the address of frame object O at offset k' once, from the entry stack root that r2ssa already computes (DecompilePrepFacts.entry_stack_address_roots), mapped to O by the P4 partition. Give every stack-pointer carrier value with such a root an inline address disposition (`&O` or `(char*)&O + k`) in the r2dec binding plan, never Bound. Treat a data read of it in the stack.rs geometry certificate like the address operand of an `lea`: the use leaves the geometry, the carrier does not. The IntSub/CallRestore chain then stays elided geometry, and the absorption at mod.rs:3070-3098 no longer sees a spelled binding. Behaviour test in crates/r2engine/tests/native.rs (byte-literal program): the gcc -O1 `rows[0]=&zero; ld(rows,0); ld(rows,1)` case renders with `rows[0] = &zero`, plus a tests/equiv `equal` for all three corpus records. Complexity: one O(1) lookup of the entry root per data use of an SP-rooted value. No new walk.

title: NEW-4: one Unimplemented/CpuId/New op anywhere in a function vetoes every entry-relative stack root, so frame carriers cannot be absorbed and the journal fails (UnownedBindingSymbol)
owner: r2ssa (function/rewrite.rs:546-556, the entry-stack-root seeding of DecompilePrepFacts; the P4 frame-partition input)
evidence: crates/r2ssa/src/function/rewrite.rs:546-556 computes entry_stack_roots_are_stable as false when any block contains `SSAOp::Unimplemented | SSAOp::CpuId { .. } | SSAOp::New { .. }`. When it is false, entry_stack_address_size stays None and no version-0 carrier gets an entry root (rewrite.rs:565-605). For gcc-O1 value_count_bits the trace reports 'call at (0x40170e, 405) found RSP_9, which has no entry-relative root ... the function has 0 entry-relative and 18 declared-base roots' (semantic/shared.rs:661). In r2dec that becomes 'ValueId(73) bound to BindingId(1) is not absorbed: no entry root' (observation_journal/mod.rs:3095), and the seal fails with UnownedBindingSymbol (sealing.rs:477). gcc-O2 has the same trace, with every call's RSP unrooted. The veto is function-wide and positional facts do not matter. The op has no output in SSA, so it cannot sit on the RSP def chain. An Unimplemented that internal_control substitutes for a local branch belongs to an instruction whose register writes are all explicit in the surrounding ops, and CpuId writes only EAX/EBX/ECX/EDX. So one `cpuid` or one bit-scan deletes the frame geometry of the entire function. This is why NEW-1 appears as a journal failure rather than an effect-obligation refusal on gcc -O1/-O2, and it would persist after NEW-1 is residualised under decision 3.
fix: Make the veto per instruction and per carrier. The lift attaches to Unimplemented the instruction's known write set: complete when internal_control produced it, unknown only for a failed decode. CpuId states its fixed outputs. entry_stack_roots_are_stable becomes false only when an op's write set is unknown or overlaps a frame carrier (the stack pointer or the frame pointer). Even then, only roots reached through that op's successors lose their entry root, not the whole function. Test: a byte-literal program in crates/r2engine/tests/native.rs with `sub rsp,8; call f; cpuid; call f` renders with the RSP chain elided. After NEW-1, value_count_bits gcc-O1 renders. Complexity: unchanged, one O(ops) scan.

title: A zeroing idiom that overwrites every lane of an entry register still reads the entry value (xorps/pxor x,x; pinsr pairs), because the only rule for it (zero_scratch_insert_roots) runs once, before the folds that expose it
owner: r2ssa: the PE dep relation in deadphi.rs gets an exact Insert transfer; the machine projection/folder narrows covered insert chains; function/rewrite.rs zero_scratch_insert_roots is deleted
evidence: The underlying gap is known: critique:lowering#4 and #1 found no Insert transfer in deadphi.rs:206-254. What is new is that this shape traps rather than just adding noise, and the phase-ordering defect behind it. Sleigh lifts `xorps xmm0,xmm0` as four lane writes `XMM0_Dx = XMM0_Dx ^ XMM0_Dx`, and rename builds INSERT^4(XMM0_0, ...). optimize.rs:1796 (`_ if a == b => make_const(0)`) folds each lane to 0. zero_scratch_insert_roots (r2ssa/src/function/rewrite.rs:26) runs only once, at r2ssa/src/function/build.rs:576, before that fold. At that point the lane Subpiece reads of XMM0_0 are ScratchUse::Observed, so the root is never zeroed. Those Subpieces are dead after the fold but stay in the prepared SSA (pdim @ 0x401420), so running the rule again would not help. No fold drops the root of an insert chain whose windows cover it: optimize.rs:1693 only reads a Subpiece through an Insert. r2dec then renders `XMM0_1 = (r2sleigh_residual_u128(1) & ~mask) | 0 ...` from Held XMM0_0. Reproduced at b1c6b637 in three places: branchy clang-O1/O2 main; scratchpad rt_probe/yns (`struct p z={0,0}; use(&z);`, -O1 -no-pie); and rt_probe/wns, where an inline-asm `xorps xmm2,xmm2` (not an ABI carrier) gives f the same residual chain. The same binary's pinsrq pair in g gives `tmp_lane = (uint64_t)(r2sleigh_residual_u128(2) >> 64)`, so the abi_carriers exclusion is not the cause. The heuristic is also itself a fake-value substitution. Its premise, 'no compiled program depends on them', is not a proof. When a partial insert chain over an unread register is stored whole, the uncovered lanes are observed caller bytes, and the rule renders them as 0.
fix: Invariant: a value whose bytes do not depend on the unspecified entry root does not read that root; one whose observed bytes do depend on it reads an Unspecified leaf (P1), never a fabricated 0. Derive this from the PE dep(op, out_byte) relation. The exact Insert transfer takes the window bytes from the inserted value and the outside bytes from the root; with byte-unaligned positions, both inputs feed the partial byte. Add a forward definedness closure. In the projection/folder, rewrite an insert chain restricted to its observed bytes into a root-free Piece or constant. This generalises critique:lowering#4's 'an INSERT whose root contributes no observed byte is its lane' to multi-insert chains. Iterate it with the other folds and DCE rather than running it once at build. Then delete zero_scratch_insert_roots. Cost is O(V+E) over the SSA graph, with byte masks of at most 64 bits, each growing monotonically. Add the per-op proof harness (exhaustive at 8/16 bits, Kani at 32/64), since the transfer becomes load-bearing for elision.

title: Callee facts are one level deep. A callee is prepared against imports only, so a callee whose result is a local call's result is Unproven, and the F15 mint proxy then drops its whole interface: silent under-arity in non-recursive chains, residual returns in mutual recursion. The result proof is also not closed over merges.
owner: r2engine: native.rs read_callees/prepare_callee compute callee facts bottom-up over call-graph SCCs, memoised per Revision. r2ssa: recover_interface runs an optimistic SCC result fixpoint and closes returned_by_call over phis. r2source: the callee contract keeps its result state separate from the parameter contract (critique:calls F15).
evidence: (1) prepare_callee (r2engine/src/native.rs:609-657) calls declare_imports and then prepare_restated(&walked, &imports, Vec::new(), declared, &[]); its doc says 'against no callee body of its own'. Any call from a callee to a local function therefore gets the convention-fallback boundary with no result (boundaries.rs:1128 'interface=false ... results=0') and is Unstated (recover_interface.rs:629). A callee that returns that CallDefine directly has an Unproven result (:749). (2) r2engine CalleeFacts::derive tries body_proven_return (lib.rs:1365-1376), but it cannot upgrade an Unproven interface: return_registers() is empty for Unproven (r2ssa/src/machine_context.rs:199-200), so the live-out it reads is empty. (3) At the caller, mint_recovered_call_site_interface refuses an Unproven callee (recover_interface.rs:1505-1511, 'call-site-minting'; critique:calls F15). The call falls back to the convention: arguments are counted from caller writes and results=0. Non-recursive repro, scratchpad scc_probe/c.c, gcc -O1 -no-pie -fno-stack-protector, stripped: h(x,y){return f(x,y)+3;}, where f returns g(x+1,y) through `call g; ret`. `pdd @ 0x401184` renders `uint64_t fcn_401184(void)` with `uint64_t RAX_1 = fcn_401168(); return RAX_1 + 3;` and the proof line '0 refused'. f's two parameters are silently dropped, which is wrong C by inspection. The trace shows 'call-site-minting ... unproven' and 'register parameters [] from reads [(32, 8)]'. In the census, shapes.c gcc-O1 shape_recurse_mutual is rated 'equal' but declares `uint64_t fcn_401845(uint64_t)` and calls it without b. It most likely passes only because the compiled rendering leaves b in RSI, since the gate does not clobber argument registers that a rendered call leaves unclaimed. (4) Mutual recursion (gcc-O1 shape_mutual_even/odd, residual-trap): the root declares the partner `void` (calls.rs:264 CExternDecl ret_type Void), and its own returned CallDefine is Unstated, so every return is a residual. (5) Merge hole: returned_by_call (recover_interface.rs:576-631) treats any live-out that is not directly a CallDefine as Produced. At -O0, `RAX_10 = phi(RAX_2, RAX_9=CALLDEF)` (pdim @ 0x401c4a, gcc-O0 shape_mutual_odd) therefore proves a Register result on an unstated premise, which is why the -O0 builds are 'equal' while -O1 traps.
fix: Invariant: a function's result is proven iff its carrier is defined on every return path, given the results of its callees. Within one call-graph SCC this is the greatest fixpoint. Start optimistic, assuming each member's convention result, re-prove every member, and retract on failure. The lattice {Unproven < Register} is finite and retraction is monotone, so this needs at most |SCC| rounds. Soundness follows by induction on the depth of terminating recursion. Plan correction: P7's 'interprocedural least fixpoint' is right for caller demand, but a least fixpoint from Unproven never proves a mutually recursive result. Prepare callee facts bottom-up over the SCC condensation (Tarjan, O(V+E)), memoised per Revision (plan P6), so a callee is prepared against its own callees' facts rather than imports only. Make returned_by_call a join over phis/copies, so a live-out that merges an Unstated CallDefine is Unstated. Per F15, give the callee contract a result state separate from its parameters, so an Unproven result still mints the proven parameters and the call is never declared `void`; the result stays a visible residual only where it is used. Delete r2engine body_proven_return (already slated in P7). Gate ratchet: the link-map shim should clobber argument registers that the rendered call does not claim before forwarding to the original callee, so a dropped pass-through argument shows up as 'differs'. Cost: O(V+E) for the condensation, plus per SCC at most |SCC| re-proofs of each member's O(|body|) live-out walk.
